walkthroughs.body_html: The Saros cycle is roughly 18 years, 11 days, 8 hours. After one Saros, similar eclipses repeat, just shifted around the globe.
Astronomers know exactly where the Moon and Sun are. They calculate when the shadow lands on Earth — predicting eclipses centuries in advance.
Solar and lunar eclipses each happen at least twice a year worldwide, but a total solar eclipse at any one place is rare — perhaps once in a lifetime.
